title: A team without GitHub tracks its specs in committed files

statements.says: A team whose remote is not GitHub can still split a spec into tickets and run the loop over them.
The tracker setting in loop.json is either github or files.
With files, each spec is a folder under .specs/ holding a spec.md, and each ticket is a file of its own in the spec's tickets folder.
A ticket file carries frontmatter for its status, its blockers and who claimed it.
The .specs/ folder is committed, and setup says it cannot be gitignored.
A ticket is closed in the same commit as its code.
A claim on a ticket is a pushed commit, so a lost push race is what stops two loops taking the same ticket.
The repo needs a remote, of any kind.
Setup refuses a repo with no remote and says how to add one: a bare repo on a shared drive is enough.
Each job builds in a worktree of its own, and a worktree cannot see a gitignored folder in the main checkout.
With the files committed, a ticket cannot be closed without Landing, because the close shares a commit with the code.
With the files committed, every teammate reads the same state.

Gitignoring .specs/ so spec text stays out of history was rejected, because it works for one person on one machine only: every job would write outside its own worktree to close its ticket, a close could not share a commit with its code, and no claim would hold.
Keeping the files for splitting only and leaving the loop on GitHub was rejected, because it does not let a team off GitHub run the loop, which is the point.
Putting every ticket in its spec's one file was rejected, because two jobs closing two tickets would edit one file at once and every landing would meet a conflict.
Allowing a repo with no remote was rejected, because worktrees, landing, claims and the grill's push would each need a second path, and one command gives any team a remote.
